Contributing to crywolf

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution. crywolf fits Bayesian false-positive occupancy models, so changes to the model or its defaults are reviewed for their statistical consequences as well as for their code.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue at https://github.com/diogoprov/crywolf/issues. A useful report has:

  • a minimal reproducible example, ideally with simulated data from simulate_fp() (the reprex package helps);
  • the output of sessionInfo() and of cmdstanr::cmdstan_version();
  • for a fit that behaves oddly, the sampler diagnostics printed by print(fit) and the call that produced it.

Questions about how to use the models for a given design are welcome as issues too.

Proposing a change

  1. Open an issue first for anything beyond a typo or a small bug fix, so that we can agree on the approach before you write code.
  2. Fork the repository and create a branch from main.
  3. Follow the existing style: tidyverse style, the native pipe |>, and roxygen2 documentation with Markdown. Internal functions get a short roxygen comment with @noRd.
  4. Add tests with testthat for every change in behaviour. Tests that fit a model need CmdStan and are skipped on CRAN; the slow statistical tests run only with CRYWOLF_EXTENDED_TESTS=true (see tests/README.md).
  5. Run devtools::document(), devtools::test() and devtools::check() before opening the pull request, and add a bullet to the development section of NEWS.md.

Changes to the Stan programs

The Stan programs live in src/stan/. A change to a likelihood or a prior should come with a test that recovers known parameters from simulated data and, when it changes results, a note in NEWS.md. The interface promises in help("crywolf-api") apply: stable arguments, classes and result names change only in a major version.

Code of conduct

Please be respectful and constructive in issues and pull requests. Contributors are expected to follow the Contributor Covenant.
